title: Manage-sell-offer with offer ID 2^53+1 passed as a native number: exact or refused
caps_note: offerID has been an int64 since the first protocol; the rule is in the XDR definitions and stellar-core's ManageOffer validation, not in a CAP.
why: 2^53+1 is a valid offer ID but not a safe IEEE-754 double: a JavaScript number literal is already 9007199254740992 before the SDK sees it, so an SDK must encode the exact ID or refuse the number.

known_divergences.detail: Executed on 17.2.0 and 17.2.1: Operation.manageSellOffer accepts the unsafe integer and encodes offer ID 9007199254740992; 17.3.0 refuses the value (fix pull request #1780).
known_divergences.evidence: probe vector 2o1 (evidence/sdk-matrix), executed on js 17.2.0 and js 17.2.1; xcc conform run --columns 'js@*' --entries 'classic/api-offer-id-encoding.id-2-pow-53-plus-1-number'

known_divergences.detail: Executed on 16.3.0, 16.3.1 and 16.4.1: Operation.manageSellOffer accepts the unsafe integer and encodes offer ID 9007199254740992. The 17.3.0 fix is not on the 16.x line.
known_divergences.evidence: probe vector 2o1 (evidence/sdk-matrix), executed on js 16.3.0 and js 16.3.1 and js 16.4.1; xcc conform run --columns 'js@*' --entries 'classic/api-offer-id-encoding.id-2-pow-53-plus-1-number'

notes: Built by xdrcheck-corpus synth from corpus/recipes/classic/api-offer-id-encoding.id-2-pow-53-plus-1-number.json. Origin: probe vector 2o1, in evidence/sdk-matrix/vectors/vectors.json, executed in every probe column (evidence/sdk-matrix). Exact or refuse: either offer ID 9007199254740993 read back and the Operation XDR (no source; MANAGE_SELL_OFFER; selling native; buying USD:GA7QYNF7…; amount 10000000 stroops; price 1/1; the ID), or a refusal. The JavaScript defect (js-stellar-sdk#1785) is the encoding of 9007199254740992 instead. Expected values were computed from the XDR definitions, the CAP or SEP text and the stellar-core rule cited under related, with an independent encoder; no SDK output was used.
